title: Universal scaling of fluctuations and correlations across the superfluid transition
authors: Paul Paquiez, Géraud Dupuy, Maxime Allemand, Henri Coquinot, Tommaso Roscilde, Nicolas Dupuis, Adam Rançon, Thomas Chalopin, David Clément
abstract: The critical behavior of a system near a continuous phase transition is commonly characterized by power laws and a set of universal critical exponents. Yet universality at phase transitions has even more fundamental manifestations. It dictates that all observables follow universal scaling functions, which may extend beyond simple power laws. Furthermore, microscopic details are captured entirely by only two system-specific scale factors, that rescale any measured quantity onto its universal form. In this work, we report the experimental validation of this prediction in ultracold lattice Bose gases undergoing the superfluid transition. We extract the scale factors by collapsing the order-parameter cumulants measured at varying entropies. We show that these factors specify scaling functions governing both the order-parameter distribution and two-point correlations. By measuring these scaling functions, we also determine three critical exponents $β$, $γ$ and $ν$. Our results provide an experimental demonstration that universal scaling is simultaneously obeyed by multiple observables in a quantum many-body system.
summary: This work experimentally verifies the concept of two-scale-factor universality near a superfluid phase transition in ultracold lattice Bose gases. By collapsing measurements of order-parameter fluctuations and correlations using two scale factors, the authors confirm that multiple observables obey the same universal scaling laws. This provides strong evidence for the deep underlying principles governing critical behavior in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: To experimentally validate the prediction of 'two-scale-factor universality' for observables across a continuous phase transition, specifically the superfluid transition.
main_result: The study demonstrated that fluctuations (cumulants) and two-point correlations simultaneously collapse onto universal scaling functions using only two entropy-dependent scale factors.
method: The authors measured order-parameter cumulants and two-point correlations in ultracold lattice Bose gases and collapsed the data using scaling theory concepts.
model_or_system: The system is ultracold lattice Bose gases modeled by the Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian, studied near the superfluid transition point.
key_observables: Order-parameter cumulants ($\kappa_n$), order-parameter probability distribution $P(|\psi|)$, and two-point correlation function $G^{(1)}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x}', u)$.
important_parameters: The control parameter is $u = U/J$, and the analysis is performed along isentropic trajectories at varying entropies.
main_assumptions: The results provide an experimental test of universality for a finite-size system, assuming corrections to classical scaling are negligible.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the concept of two-scale-factor universality, showing the collapse of bare cumulants onto universal curves using scale factors A and B, and displaying the scaling of the order parameter PDF and correlation length.
paper_structure:
The paper introduces the concept of universal scaling, presents experimental measurements of cumulants and correlations across the superfluid transition, demonstrates the collapse onto universal functions using two scale factors, and finally determines critical exponents ($ eta, \gamma, 
u$).
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, quantitative experimental test of fundamental concepts in critical phenomena—specifically, the simultaneous universality of multiple observables—in a highly controllable quantum many-body platform.
